extracted.intended_audience: readers of a progressive early-20th-century women's magazine; suffragists and general readers interested in social criticism
extracted.subtask_description: An early-20th-century editorial/essay arguing that politics and warfare are products of androcentric culture, with prescriptive claims about how politics, education, and society should be reorganized and how women should be included. Mixes social critique, book review recommendations, and practical domestic advice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dictionary definition of politics (purpose of government)
rubrics_metrics.description: Politics: The science of government; that part of ethics which has to do with the regulation and government of a nation or state, the preservation of its safety, peace and prosperity; the defence of its existence and rights against foreign control or conquest; the augmentation of its strength and resources, and the protection of its citizens in their rights; with the preservation and improvement of their morals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as the working statement of what politics should aim to do; frames subsequent argument that politics is properly an ethical/scientific endeavor rather than a fight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Politics as part of ethics (science of conduct)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ethics is the science of conduct, and politics is merely one field of conduct; a very common one.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implication: political activity should be guided by ethical standards (preservation of safety, prosperity, protection of citizens, moral improvement) rather than masculine/combative instincts. This recasts politics as compatible with caregiving/administrative values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Politics should be dissociated from warfare
rubrics_metrics.description: There are many to-day who hold that politics need not be at all connected with warfare, and others who hold that politics is warfare front start to finish. In order to dissociate the two ideas completely ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Politics ought not to be treated as continual combat; it should be organized around governance, welfare, and administration rather than military-style struggle. The essay repeatedly insists that conflating politics with warfare produces injustice and bad governance.

rubrics_metrics.name: The science of politics ought to be taught simply and practically in schools
rubrics_metrics.description: The science of politics, in a civilized community, should have by this time a fine accumulation of simplified knowledge for diffusion in public schools; a store of practical experience in how to promote social advancement most rapidly, a progressive economy and ease of administration, a simplicity in theory and visible benefit in practice, such as should make every child an eager and serviceable citizen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prescriptive standard for civic education: politics should be systematized into teachable, practical knowledge to cultivate competent citizens, not left as an arena of manipulation and party fighting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Party system critique — parties are technical arrangements for fighting
rubrics_metrics.description: We find first a party system which is the technical arrangement to carry on a fight. It is perfectly conceivable that a flourishing democratic government be carried on without any parties at all; public functionaries being elected on their merits, and each proposed measure judged on its merits;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluative criterion: a healthy democracy might select officials and measures on merit rather than through adversarial party machinery. The party-as-fight model is presented as an androcentric artifact to be rethought.

rubrics_metrics.name: Women are needed in politics; exclusion is unjustified
rubrics_metrics.description: Few men can overlook the limitations of their sex and see the truth; that this business of taking care of our common affairs is not only equally open to women and men, but that women are distinctly needed in it. The inextricable confusion of politics and warfare is part of the stumbling block in the minds of men ... 'women cannot fight, therefore they cannot vote.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argument against the standard objection that inability to fight disqualifies women politically. Prescriptive: enfranchisement and political participation are necessary and beneficial; women's skills and perspectives are required for better governance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Military ideals and methods corrupt political and social ethics
rubrics_metrics.description: An androcentric culture has always exempted its own essential activities from the restraints of ethics,--'All's fair in love and war!' Deceit, trickery, lying, every kind of skulking underhand effort to get information; ceaseless endeavor to outwit and overcome 'the enemy' ... as well as the much praised virtues of courage, endurance and loyalty, personal and public. Also classed as a virtue ... is that prime factor ... obedience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluative standard: political and civic institutions should not normalize military virtues (deceit, underhand tactics, blind obedience). Instead, governance should favor honesty, efficiency, wisdom, experience and love; military methods are inappropriate templates for civil administration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Warfare damages civilization — four primary harms
rubrics_metrics.description: The external horrors and wastes of warfare ... A. It arrests industry and all progress. B. It destroys the fruits of industry and progress. C. It weakens, hurts and kills the combatants. D. It lowers the standard of the non-combatants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these fourfold criteria to judge the social cost of war: interruptions to industry and progress; destruction of accumulated goods; debilitation or death of those used as combatants; and moral/standard decline among those left at home. The essay treats these as decisive negatives against idealizing warfare.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combat as biological selection is maladaptive socially
rubrics_metrics.description: Combat is a physical process, ... intended to improve the species by the elimination of the unfit. ... when applied to society, it eliminates the fit, and leaves the unfit to perpetuate the race! We require, to do our organized fighting, a picked lot of vigorous young males ... the pick of the country, physically, is sent off to oppose the pick of another country, and kill--kill--kill!
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion for assessing warfare's eugenic/ demographic impact: organized fighting removes the best reproductive stock from civilian life, lowers birth-rate and 'quality' at home, spreads disease, and produces long-term social injury.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultural valorization of soldiers over productive workers is misplaced
rubrics_metrics.description: The monuments to soldiers and sailors ... still go up, and the tin soldier remains a popular toy. We do not see boxes of tin carpenters by any chance; tin farmers, weavers, shoemakers; we do not write our 'boys books' about the real benefactors and servers of society; the adventurer and destroyer remains the idol of an Androcentric Culture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluative standard for cultural recognition: societies should honor productive, peace-building labor and service (farmers, artisans, teachers) rather than glamorizing warriors and adventurers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peace activism alone is insufficient while militaristic symbols persist
rubrics_metrics.description: Peace congresses have begun to meet, peace societies write and talk, but the monuments to soldiers and sailors ... still go up ... the adventurer and destroyer remains the idol.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guideline: meaningful cultural change requires not only peace societies but also removal or rebalancing of public symbols that glorify war; otherwise the militaristic mindset endures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewing/publishing duty: magazines should keep useful book lists and call attention to important ideas
rubrics_metrics.description: We mean to carry lists of books useful to our readers. We wish to prove that it will pay publishers to advertise with us. There is a book which ought to be held in continual prominence by every magazine in the world that appeals particularly to women ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical standard for editors/publishers: actively promote and repeatedly highlight works of major importance (even if contemporary reviewers miss their long-range significance); use reviews and lists to educate readers and stimulate study groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to handle incompatibility between an aged mother and married daughter
rubrics_metrics.description: If the daughter allows her irritation and critical attitude to result in actual discussion and expressed disapproval ... she is certainly to blame. ... The Practical Answer ... She can (a) alter her ways; (b) live somewhere else; (c) ... put it clearly to the daughter, 'as man to man,' that she has to live with her, that she cannot learn new ways, and that they must use mutual politeness ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical domestic guideline: resolve intergenerational incompatibility by self-change, relocation, or setting clear, mutually polite boundaries; avoid assuming 'blame'—focus on workable arrangements and mutual accommodation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Centralized (large) kitchens reduce flies and improve sanitation
rubrics_metrics.description: One kitchen, though large, is more easily protected than a hundred kitchens, though small. ... in such a kitchen there will be no laundry or other extraneous work done; no running in and out of children and others; nothing but the scientific preparation of food. Also ... the flies will be reduced 99 per cent. by the reduction in the number of horses required to bring supplies and remove garbage and ashes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical public-health criterion: centralizing food preparation under properly managed facilities reduces vectors (flies), improves cleanliness, and permits higher-grade officers to maintain sanitation; supports arguments for domestic/municipal reform of kitchen and supply arrangements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical remedy for a wife whose small independent expenditures are cut by husband
rubrics_metrics.description: The best answer is: let the woman EARN HER OWN LIVING. That goes farthest in changing self-sacrifice to justice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prescriptive social-economic standard: economic independence for women is the primary means to transform perceived 'virtue' of self-sacrifice into a sense of justice and fair personal agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize that reviewers may miss long-range importance of works
rubrics_metrics.description: When I read it I was so impressed with its colossal possibility that I went to the publishers and asked to see the reviews—expecting to find some recognition of a world-lifting truth. I found nothing of the sort. The reviewers reviewed the book in general with respect ... not one recognized its measureless importance. This is not remarkable. In proportion to the far-reaching value of a truth is the difficulty of popular recognition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guideline for critics and editors: be cautious about mistaking lack of immediate popular recognition for lack of importance; cultivate judgment that can perceive long-term significance and promote such works accordingly.
